title: Monthly Salary Calculator Australia: Convert Hourly Pay to Annual, Fortnightly & Tax
description: Use our monthly salary calculator Australia to convert hourly rates to annual, fortnightly, and monthly pay. Includes 38-hour week, super, tax, and state earnings differences.
salarySummary: Annual pay is hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming a standard 38-hour week for full-time work.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary using the monthly salary calculator Australia?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52. The monthly salary calculator Australia on this site does this for you, and also shows fortnightly pay, tax, and super.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include casual loading and superannuation?
faqs.a: Yes. There is a checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. Superannuation is calculated at 12% of ordinary earnings and is paid on top of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. The calculator does not assume your rate already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: Why do state differences in ordinary-time earnings matter when using the calculator?
faqs.a: The calculator uses a national average for tax and super, but your actual earnings may differ by state. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full-time adult ordinary-time earnings vary across states – for example, the ACT tends to have higher average weekly earnings than Tasmania. The calculator gives an estimate; for your specific award or industry, check the relevant pay guide on our site.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

Whether you are an employee on an award rate or a contractor negotiating a salary, the **monthly salary calculator Australia** on this page helps you see the full picture. Enter your base hourly rate, choose whether to add casual loading, and the calculator instantly shows your annual, fortnightly, and monthly gross pay, along with estimated tax and superannuation.

### The Core Formula

Annual gross pay is calculated as:

**hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a standard full-time week, we assume 38 hours – the ordinary hours defined by the Fair Work Act. If you work different hours, you can adjust the weekly hours in the calculator. The result is your annual salary before tax, Medicare levy, and super.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. Many employees are covered by award rates that are higher than the minimum. The **monthly salary calculator Australia** lets you enter any hourly rate, but remember that your actual minimum entitlement may be set by your award or enterprise agreement.

### Fortnightly and Monthly Pay

If you are paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For example, a full-time worker on the minimum wage earns $1,004.90 per week, so their fortnightly gross is $2,009.80. Monthly pay is roughly weekly × 52 ÷ 12, but the calculator shows an exact monthly figure based on the annual amount divided by 12.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your gross pay. This is not deducted from your salary – it is an additional contribution. The super guarantee has a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. If your annual ordinary earnings exceed that, super is only paid on the first $270,830. The calculator includes this limit.

### Tax and Medicare

For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian Taxation Office resident tax rates are:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare (as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this estimate). It does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice arrangements.

### State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) data. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary-time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week nationally. However, this figure varies by state and territory. For example, the ACT often records higher average earnings due to a concentration of public sector and professional roles, while Tasmania and South Australia tend to be lower. The **monthly salary calculator Australia** uses a national tax and super framework, but your actual earnings may differ depending on where you work. For a more tailored estimate, check the relevant award or industry pay guide.

### Using the Calculator Responsibly

This tool provides an estimate only. It assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings up to the maximum contribution base. Tax is based on the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Always consult your employer, a registered tax agent, or the Fair Work Ombudsman for a binding determination of your pay.

Whether you are comparing a salary offer or planning your budget, the **monthly salary calculator Australia** is your starting point for understanding the full value of your hourly rate.
